subtitle: A translation guide, not a SQL course

code:
-- T-SQL
SELECT TOP 10 customer_id, order_total
FROM orders
ORDER BY order_total DESC;

-- Snowflake
SELECT customer_id, order_total
FROM orders
ORDER BY order_total DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- Concatenation
first_name || ' ' || last_name   -- Snowflake
first_name + ' ' + last_name     -- T-SQL
caption: LIMIT goes at the end of the query; || is Snowflake's concatenation operator.

eyebrow: IFF() vs. IIF()  ·  CASE is unchanged
code:
-- T-SQL
SELECT IIF(order_total > 100, 'Large', 'Small')
FROM orders;

-- Snowflake
SELECT IFF(order_total > 100, 'Large', 'Small')
FROM orders;

-- CASE works identically in both dialects
CASE WHEN order_total > 500 THEN 'Large'
     WHEN order_total > 100 THEN 'Medium'
     ELSE 'Small' END
caption: IFF is IIF with one fewer letter. Full CASE needs no changes at all.

code:
-- T-SQL needs a wrapping CTE
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
    PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC) AS rn
  FROM orders
)
SELECT * FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1;

-- Snowflake filters the window function directly
SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
  PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC) AS rn
FROM orders
QUALIFY rn = 1;
caption: QUALIFY is the window-function equivalent of HAVING — no CTE required.
